SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL C. I. D. REGISTRY
[June 5th, 1930.] No. I. O. U. / 353.
Date 15....6.. 30.

THE JAPAN WEEKLY CHRONICLE.

PROTEST BY LABOUR.

THE NEW WEAPON OF THE TOKYO
POLICE.

The Labour leaders in Tokyo strongly resent the use of the tear-gas revolvers by the police in dispersing the Tokyo tramway employees who assembled near Hibiya for demonstration on the 26th ultimo, as already reported. On the 27th ultimo, the Central Executive Committee of the Shakai Minshuto, a Labour party, met to discuss the matter, as the result of which it was agreed that a strong protest should be entered with the Chief of the Metropolitan Police. The leaders of the Shakai Minshuto contend that the use of tear-gas revolvers against those participating in legitimate social movements is tantamount to viewing such movements in the same criminal light as burglaries and murders, and that such behaviour on the part of the police is destined to drive social movements into dangerous channels. They have decided to demand that the policemen who abuse this weapon should be severely punished.

The Central Executive Committee of the Nihon Taishuto, another Labour party, also met on the same day, when a similar decision was reached against the use of the weapon by the police. The party was to send a delegation to the Metropolitan Police Board on the 28th to file a strong protest on the ground that the use of tear-gas revolvers against labour demonstrators threatens to usher in an age of armed conflict in industrial disputes. The leaders of the party strongly dispute the legal grounds on which the use of such revolvers was permitted by the police authorities.

We cull from the Japan Times the following account of the affair:—

The conflict arose as a result of a mass parade started by the tram and bus operatives including 150 women workers toward noon Monday for the purpose of pressing their demand to have their fellow workers who had been dismissed by the city authorities due to their aggressive participation in the last tram and bus strike reinstated in their former posts. As Mayor Horikiri and Mr. Kakei, head of the Electric Bureau, have both resigned the workers decided to carry out a manifestation so that their demand might be kept up as an open issue. Before resorting to the tactic they definitely disavowed any intention to go on another general strike.

Further, as a proper precaution prior to their demonstration the agitators' delegates laid their plan before the Chief of the Metropolitan Police, Mr. Maruyama, who told them that they had better give up the scheme. Disregarding the official's explicit warning the movement was begun by approximately 1,000 workers who gathering near Hibiya Park made for the Electric Bureau building at Marunouchi in an orderly procession at first.

Soon orderliness, however, gave way to something akin to a riot when the police strove to stem the march at the entrance of the Electric Bureau. At a sign given by a commander of the police brigade the officers whipped out the gas pistols and showered chemical shots at the crowd bringing down dozens of men instantly. A terrific stampede followed. The fallen comrades were carried to the neighbouring hospitals in an unconscious state. As the doctors knew nothing of the new fangled weapons, they were at first at a loss to ascertain the cause of the troubles of the patients. After two or three hours the patients came to themselves.

CHIEF OF POLICE APOLOGISES.

About twenty representatives of the Shakai Minshuto, the Nihon Taishuto, the Ronoto, the Tokyo Proletarian Party, and the Tokyo Communications Labour Union visited Mr. Maruyama, Chief of the Metropolitan Police, on the 28th ultimo and filed a joint protest against the use of tear-gas revolvers by the Hibiya police against the members of the Tokyo Communications Labour Union, who made a demonstration near Hibiya Park on the 26th. In reply, Mr. Maruyama said that the action of the Hibiya police on the occasion left something to be desired, and assured the delegation that he would see that tear-gas revolvers were used as little as possible in future in connection with the control of labour movements.

The labour representatives were to visit Mr. Adachi, the Home Minister, on Thursday (29th ultimo) and lodge a similar protest about the matter.

THE Police Bureau, it is announced, do not consider the tear-gas revolver as a weapon. Presumably, therefore, anybody may carry one without a licence and their discharge at any one is not an offence but something in the shape of a practical joke. Whether an instrument is a weapon or not depends upon the use to which it is put. It is not illegal to carry a penknife but it is certainly illegal to use it as a weapon to stab people. Many other articles of everyday use can be turned into weapons on occasion, including the geta, which is indeed a favourite weapon with the lower classes in Japan. But all these articles can be put to other and harmless uses. The tear-gas pistol cannot, unless the laying out of an occasional burglar can be so considered. Even then it is to be feared that the burglar would decide it was a weapon and a very nasty one. To try to make out that the pistol is not a weapon would therefore seem to open the way to wholesale sale without a licence and indiscriminate use by footpads in quiet places. It is a weapon and nothing else, even if its use does not involve death, and should certainly be licensed.

上海公共租界工部局警务处刑事调查科档案室
[1930年6月5日。] 编号 I. O. U. / 353。
日期 1930年6月15日。

《日本纪事周刊》。

劳工的抗议。

东京警方的新武器。

正如前文所报道，东京的劳工领袖对警方在上月26日驱散聚集在日比谷附近进行示威的东京电车员工时使用催泪瓦斯左轮手枪的行为表示强烈愤慨。上月27日，劳工政党社会民众党（Shakai Minshuto）中央执行委员会召开会议讨论此事，结果决定向警视总监提出强烈抗议。社会民众党的领导人声称，对参与合法社会运动的人士使用催泪瓦斯左轮手枪，无异于将此类运动视为与入室盗窃和谋杀同等的犯罪行为，而警方的这种行为注定会将社会运动推向危险的渠道。他们已决定要求严惩滥用此武器的警察。

另一劳工政党日本大众党（Nihon Taishuto）的中央执行委员会也在同日召开会议，针对警方使用该武器作出了类似的决定。该党计划于28日派遣代表团前往警视厅，以警方对劳工示威者使用催泪瓦斯左轮手枪恐将开启劳资纠纷中武装冲突时代为由，提出强烈抗议。该党领导人强烈质疑警方当局允许使用此类左轮手枪的法律依据。

我们从《日本时报》摘录了以下关于此事的报道：—

冲突起因于周一中午前后，由包括150名女工在内的电车和巴士操作员发起的大规模游行，目的是施压要求市政府恢复那些因积极参与上次电车和巴士罢工而被解雇的同事的原职。由于堀切市长和电气局局长挂井先生均已辞职，工人们决定举行示威活动，以便使他们的诉求作为一个公开议题持续下去。在采取这一策略之前，他们明确否认有任何发动另一次总罢工的意图。

此外，作为示威前的适当预防措施，煽动者的代表向警视总监丸山先生陈述了他们的计划，丸山先生告诉他们最好放弃该计划。示威者无视官员的明确警告，约1000名工人开始了行动，他们最初在日比谷公园附近集结，然后排成有序的队伍向丸之内的电气局大楼进发。

然而，当警方试图在电气局入口处阻止游行队伍时，秩序很快让位于近乎暴乱的场面。随着警察大队指挥官发出信号，警官们拔出瓦斯手枪，向人群发射化学弹药，瞬间击倒数十人。随后发生了可怕的恐慌性奔逃。倒下的同伴被送往附近的医院时处于昏迷状态。由于医生们对这种新式武器一无所知，起初无法确定患者病痛的原因。两三个小时后，患者恢复了知觉。

示威活动的领导人立即就这种严厉惩罚向丸山先生提出了投诉——

档案。
请仔细归档。
1930年6月10日

警视总监道歉。

上月28日，社会民众党、日本大众党、劳农党（Ronoto）、东京无产阶级党和东京通讯业工会的约二十名代表拜访了警视总监丸山先生，并就日比谷警方在上月26日对日比谷公园附近示威的东京通讯业工会成员使用催泪瓦斯左轮手枪一事提出联合抗议。作为回应，丸山先生表示，日比谷警方在此事中的行为仍有不足之处，并向代表团保证，他将在未来管控劳工运动时尽量减少催泪瓦斯左轮手枪的使用。

劳工代表计划于周四（上月29日）拜访内务大臣安达先生，并就此事提出类似的抗议。

据悉，警察局并不认为催泪瓦斯左轮手枪是一种武器。因此，据推测，任何人无需执照即可携带，向任何人发射也不构成犯罪，而更像是一种恶作剧。一件器具是否属于武器，取决于其用途。携带小折刀并不违法，但将其作为刺伤他人的武器使用则肯定违法。许多其他日常用品在特定情况下也可变成武器，包括木屐（geta），这确实是日本下层阶级喜爱的一种武器。但所有这些物品都可以用于其他无害的用途。催泪瓦斯手枪却不能，除非偶尔制服窃贼可被视为无害用途。即便如此，恐怕窃贼也会认定这是一种武器，而且是一种非常令人讨厌的武器。因此，试图辩称该手枪不是武器，似乎会为无执照的大规模销售以及在僻静处被歹徒 indiscriminate（随意/不加区分地）使用打开方便之门。它是一种武器，别无其他，即使其使用不涉及致死，也绝对应当实行许可制度。
